name: Completely additive function
description: An arithmetic function f satisfying f(mn) = f(m) + f(n) for all m, n ≥ 1; equivalently f(p^a) = a·f(p), e.g. Ω(n) and log n.

name: Generalized divisor function τ_k(n)
description: τ_k(n) = ∑_{n=n₁⋯nₖ} 1, the number of ordered k-fold factorizations of n; its Dirichlet series is ζ(s)^k.

name: Selberg–Delange method
function_signature: (Dirichlet series behaving like ζ(s)^z near s=1) → (asymptotic ∑_{n≤x} a_n ~ Cx(log x)^{z-1}/Γ(z))
description: Obtains asymptotics for partial sums of Dirichlet series behaving like ζ(s)^z near s = 1 via contour integration around a Hankel contour.

name: Smoothed Perron formula
description: A variant of Perron's formula using a smooth weight function to replace the sharp cutoff, yielding faster-decaying error terms via rapid decay of the Mellin transform of the weight.

name: Dyadic decomposition
function_signature: (sum over [1,X]) → (O(log X) sums over dyadic blocks (N, 2N])
description: Partitioning a sum over [1, X] into O(log X) blocks of the form (N, 2N], reducing estimates to those uniform in a parameter N.

name: Smooth partition of unity
function_signature: (sharp cutoff) → (sum of smooth bumps with ∑ψ_j ≡ 1)
description: A collection of smooth bump functions {ψ_j} with ∑_j ψ_j ≡ 1, used to decompose sums into pieces with controlled Mellin or Fourier transforms.

name: Heath-Brown's identity
function_signature: (Λ(n) for n ≤ x) → (O(k²) multilinear Type I/II sums)
description: Decomposes the von Mangoldt function into O(k) multilinear sums using k-fold applications of an identity involving μ and log, yielding flexible Type I and Type II sums.

name: Linnik's identity
function_signature: (Λ(n)) → (alternating series of higher-order convolutions)
description: Expresses Λ(n) as Λ = ∑_{k≥1} (−1)^{k−1}/k · (1∗⋯∗1 − ε)^{∗k} · log, converting prime sums into iterated convolution sums.

name: Type I sum
description: A sum of the form ∑_{m≤M} a_m ∑_{n: mn∈A} 1 where a_m are general coefficients and the inner sum is over a well-understood sequence.

name: Type II sum
description: A bilinear sum ∑_m ∑_n a_m b_n c(mn) where both variables carry nontrivial coefficients, requiring Cauchy–Schwarz or bilinear form techniques.

name: Wirsing's theorem
description: For nonnegative multiplicative f with ∑_p f(p)/p ~ κ log log x, gives ∑_{n≤x} f(n) ~ Ce^{-γκ}/Γ(κ) · x(log x)^{κ-1} ∏_p(1+f(p)/p+⋯)(1-1/p)^κ.

name: Shiu's bound
description: For multiplicative f with 0 ≤ f(n) ≤ τ(n)^A, gives ∑_{x<n≤x+y, n≡a(q)} f(n) ≪ (y/φ(q))exp(∑_{p≤x} f(p)/p) for y ≥ x^{1/2+ε}.

name: General L-function (Iwaniec–Kowalski framework)
description: An L-function satisfying: Euler product of degree d, analytic continuation, functional equation Λ(s) = εΛ̄(1−s) with gamma factors, and the Ramanujan bound |a(p)| ≤ d.

name: Completed L-function
description: Λ(s, π) = q^{s/2} ∏_j Γ_ℝ(s + μ_j) · L(s, π) incorporating conductor q and gamma factors, satisfying Λ(s) = ε Λ̄(1−s).

name: Root number
description: The complex number ε of absolute value 1 in the functional equation Λ(s) = εΛ̄(1−s); for self-dual L-functions ε = ±1, governing vanishing at the central point.

name: Gamma factors in functional equations
description: The archimedean part γ(s) = ∏_j Γ_ℝ(s + μ_j) of a completed L-function, where Γ_ℝ(s) = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2), encoding the archimedean local factors.

name: Conductor of an L-function
description: The positive integer q(π) in the functional equation measuring arithmetic ramification; equals ∏_p p^{f_p} with f_p the local conductor exponents.

name: Analytic conductor
description: C(π) = q(π)∏_j(|μ_j|+3), the quantity governing convexity bounds, zero-free regions, and approximate functional equations of an L-function.

name: Degree of an L-function
description: The number d of Γ_ℝ-factors in the completed L-function; equals n for GL(n) automorphic L-functions, governing the growth rate and density of zeros.

name: Convexity bound for L-functions
description: For an L-function of analytic conductor C, L(1/2+it) ≪ C(t)^{1/4+ε}, obtained from the Phragmén–Lindelöf principle applied to the functional equation.

name: Subconvexity bound
description: Any bound L(1/2, π) ≪ C(π)^{1/4−δ} for some δ > 0 breaking the convexity barrier; has applications to equidistribution and mass transfer.

name: Grand Lindelöf hypothesis
description: The conjecture that L(1/2+it, π) ≪ C(π, t)^ε for every ε > 0 and every automorphic L-function; generalizes the Lindelöf hypothesis.

name: Approximate functional equation
description: L(s) = ∑_{n≤x} a_n n^{−s} V(n/x) + ε(s)∑_{n≤y} ā_n n^{s−1} W(n/y) + remainder, expressing L(s) on the critical line as two finite sums of length ~√(q|t|).

name: Mean value theorem for Dirichlet polynomials
description: ∫_0^T |∑_{n≤N} a_n n^{−it}|² dt = (T + O(N))∑|a_n|², the Montgomery–Vaughan form equating the L² norm over t to the sum of squared coefficients.

name: Montgomery's mean value theorem for large values
description: Bounds the number R of well-spaced t-values where |∑ a_n n^{−it}| ≥ V: R ≪ (N+T)(∑|a_n|²)/V², controlling large values of Dirichlet polynomials.

name: Huxley–Jutila large values estimate
description: Refined bounds on the measure of t-values where a Dirichlet polynomial is large, improving Montgomery's estimate via mean-square and fourth-power moment methods.

name: Fourth moment of the Riemann zeta function
description: ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|⁴ dt ~ (2π²)⁻¹ T(log T)⁴, proved by Ingham (1926); the highest moment of ζ(1/2+it) for which an asymptotic is known.

name: Second moment of L-functions over characters
description: ∑_{χ mod q} |L(1/2, χ)|² ~ (φ(q)/q)·q log q, the mean-square for central values of Dirichlet L-functions averaged over characters mod q.

name: Moments of L-functions (conjectural asymptotics)
description: The conjecture that ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} dt ~ c_k T(log T)^{k²} with c_k predicted by random matrix theory (Keating–Snaith).

name: Hecke L-function
description: L(s, λ) = ∑_𝔞 λ(𝔞)N(𝔞)^{−s} attached to a Hecke Grössencharakter λ of a number field, admitting Euler product, analytic continuation, and functional equation.

name: Rankin–Selberg L-function
description: L(s, π × π') = ∏_p det(I − A_π(p) ⊗ A_{π'}(p) p^{−s})^{−1}, a degree-mn L-function for GL(m)×GL(n) forms with analytic continuation and functional equation.

name: Kronecker's limit formula
description: The Laurent expansion of the Epstein zeta function at s = 1 has constant term involving −π(γ + log 2 − log(√y|η(τ)|²)), connecting Eisenstein series to the Dedekind eta function.

name: Sifting function S(A, P, z)
description: S(A, P, z) = |{a ∈ A : gcd(a, P(z)) = 1}| where P(z) = ∏_{p<z, p∈P} p, counting elements not divisible by any sifting prime below z.

name: Sieve dimension
description: The parameter κ such that ∑_{w≤p<z} g(p)log p = κ log(z/w) + O(1), governing sifting prime density; κ = 1 for the linear sieve, κ = 1/2 for binary quadratic forms.

name: Buchstab's identity
description: S(A, P, z) = S(A, P, w) − ∑_{w≤p<z} S(A_p, P, p), recursively expressing the sifting function at level z in terms of lower levels.

name: Linear sieve (Iwaniec's formulation)
description: For sieve dimension κ = 1, S(A,P,z) = X·W(z){f(s)+O((log D)^{-1/3})} with s = log D/log z, where f and F solve the linear sieve differential-delay equations.

name: Sieve upper/lower bound functions F_κ(s), f_κ(s)
description: Continuous functions satisfying differential-delay equations giving best possible sieve bounds: f_κ(s)XV(z) ≤ S ≤ F_κ(s)XV(z) + remainder.

name: Rosser–Iwaniec sieve (β-sieve)
function_signature: (sifting function S(A,P,z), level D) → (optimal upper/lower bounds)
description: A combinatorial sieve using Rosser's alternating truncation combined with Iwaniec's bilinear remainder estimates, achieving optimal bounds for the linear sieve.

name: Parity problem in sieve theory
description: The obstruction that classical sieve methods cannot distinguish integers with even vs odd number of prime factors, preventing sieves from detecting primes in the main term.

name: Semilinear sieve (κ = 1/2)
function_signature: (sieve problem of dimension 1/2) → (upper/lower bounds without parity obstruction)
description: The sieve of dimension κ = 1/2, applicable to primes represented by binary quadratic forms; the lower bound becomes positive for s > 1.

name: Bombieri's asymptotic sieve
function_signature: (sifting function with strong remainder estimates) → (asymptotic formula for primes)
description: A sieve producing asymptotic formulas for sifting functions under strong equidistribution hypotheses, overcoming the parity problem.

name: Asymptotic sieve for primes (Bombieri–Friedlander–Iwaniec)
function_signature: (sequence A with bilinear remainder control) → (asymptotic for #{primes in A})
description: Combines Bombieri's asymptotic sieve with bilinear form estimates to produce asymptotic formulas for primes in sequences, circumventing the parity problem.

name: Level of distribution
description: The supremum ϑ such that ∑_{q≤x^ϑ-ε} max_{(a,q)=1} |A(x;q,a) − A(x)/φ(q)| ≪ A(x)/(log x)^B; the primes have ϑ = 1/2 by Bombieri–Vinogradov.

name: Well-factorable function
description: A function λ(d) is well-factorable of level D if for every D = D₁D₂ there exist λ₁, λ₂ with λ = λ₁∗λ₂, |λ_i| ≤ 1, and support at scale D_i; key to Iwaniec's bilinear sieve.

name: Switching principle in sieve theory
function_signature: (upper bound sieve result) → (lower bound for primes)
description: Reversing roles of sifted set and sifting primes via Buchstab decomposition, exploiting different distributional properties to convert upper into lower bounds.

name: Van der Corput's A-process
function_signature: (exponential sum with |f''| ≍ λ) → (bound O(Nλ^{1/2} + λ^{-1/2}))
description: The second derivative test: if f'' is monotone and |f''(x)| ≍ λ, then ∑ e(f(n)) ≪ Nλ^{1/2} + λ^{-1/2}.
aliases: van der Corput second derivative test

name: Van der Corput's B-process
function_signature: (exponential sum ∑ e(f(n))) → (dual sum via Poisson summation)
description: Transforms ∑ e(f(n)) into a dual sum via Poisson summation, converting information about f' into a shorter dual sum.

name: Method of exponent pairs
function_signature: (A- and B-processes iterated) → (family of admissible exponent pairs (k,ℓ))
description: A framework for bounding exponential sums by iterating A-process (k,ℓ)→(k/(2k+2),(k+ℓ+1)/(2k+2)) and B-process (k,ℓ)→(ℓ-1/2,k+1/2).

name: Exponent pair (k, ℓ)
description: A pair (k,ℓ) such that ∑_{n~N} e(f(n)) ≪ N^ℓ λ^k when |f^(j)| ≍ λ/N^j; the trivial pair is (0,1) and (1/2,1/2) from van der Corput.

name: Vinogradov's method of exponential sums
function_signature: (exponential sum with polynomial phase of degree k) → (bound via iterated Weyl differencing + Vinogradov mean value theorem)
description: Bounds exponential sums using iterated Weyl differencing followed by Hölder's inequality and mean value estimates, producing the Vinogradov–Korobov zero-free region.

name: Salié sum
description: S*(a,b;c) = ∑_{x mod c, (x,c)=1} (x/c)e((ax+bx̄)/c), the Kloosterman sum twisted by the Legendre symbol; evaluable in terms of Gauss sums when c is prime.

name: Hyper-Kloosterman sum
description: Kl_k(a;q) = ∑_{x₁⋯x_k ≡ a(q)} e((x₁+⋯+x_k)/q), the k-variable Kloosterman sum satisfying Deligne's bound |Kl_k(a;p)| ≤ k·p^{(k-1)/2}.

name: Stepanov's method
function_signature: (curve C/𝔽_q) → (bound |C(𝔽_q)| via auxiliary polynomial)
description: An elementary method bounding rational points on curves over finite fields by constructing an auxiliary polynomial vanishing to high order at each rational point.

name: Bombieri's proof of RH for curves
description: A simplified proof of the Riemann hypothesis for curves over finite fields using Stepanov's method and Riemann-Roch, avoiding Weil's algebraic geometry.

name: Square sieve (Heath-Brown)
function_signature: (sequence S) → (bound on #{n ∈ S : n = □} via character sums)
description: Detects perfect squares in sequences via n is a square iff (n/p) = 1 for all primes p, applying Legendre symbols and the large sieve.

name: Bombieri–Iwaniec method
function_signature: (exponential sum ∑ e(f(n))) → (improved bound via lattice point/large sieve)
description: Bounds exponential sums by converting to a lattice point counting problem near a curve, then applying the large sieve to detect coincidences; yields exponent pair (9/56, 1/2+9/56).

name: Duality principle for bilinear forms
description: The operator norm of a bilinear form equals its transpose norm; in the large sieve, interchanges the roles of the sequence and test points.

name: Dual large sieve inequality
description: ∑_n |∑_r b_r e(nα_r)|² ≤ (N + δ⁻¹)∑|b_r|² for δ-spaced α_r; the dual form of the large sieve.
aliases: dual form of the large sieve

name: Large sieve inequality for Dirichlet characters
description: ∑_{q≤Q} ∑*_{χ mod q} |∑_{n≤N} a_n χ(n)|² ≤ (N + Q² − 1)∑|a_n|², bounding mean squares of character sums over primitive characters.

name: Deshouillers–Iwaniec method
function_signature: (sums of Kloosterman sums) → (bounds via spectral theory + Kuznetsov formula)
description: Combines Kloosterman sum estimates, spectral theory, and the Kuznetsov trace formula to bound bilinear forms in Kloosterman sums.

name: Linnik's dispersion method
function_signature: (sum over arithmetic progression) → (variance estimate via Cauchy-Schwarz)
description: Estimates ∑_q(∑_{n≡a(q)} f(n) − main)² by expanding the square and exchanging summation, reducing to bilinear sums.

name: Halász–Montgomery inequality
description: For R well-spaced t_r: ∑_r |∑_n a_n n^{-it_r}|² ≤ (N + RT)(∑|a_n|²), a discrete mean value theorem for Dirichlet polynomials.

name: Motohashi's formula
description: An exact identity relating the fourth moment of ζ(1/2+it) to a spectral sum over Maass forms, expressing ∫|ζ|⁴ in terms of Hecke eigenvalues.

name: Gallagher's larger sieve
description: If S ⊂ [1,N] reduces to at most ν_p residue classes mod p for each p ∈ P, then |S| ≤ N(∑ log p)/(∑ ν_p log p/(p−ν_p+1)) − corrections.

name: Barban–Davenport–Halberstam theorem
description: ∑_{q≤Q} ∑_{(a,q)=1} |ψ(x;q,a) − x/φ(q)|² ≪ xQ log x for Q ≤ x, an L² average bound on PNT errors in arithmetic progressions.

name: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture
description: The conjecture that primes have level of distribution ϑ = 1 − ε; implies bounded gaps between primes by the Goldston–Pintz–Yıldırım method.

name: Modular group SL₂(ℤ)
description: The group of 2×2 integer matrices with determinant 1, acting on the upper half-plane by Möbius transformations; the fundamental discrete symmetry group of modular forms.

name: Congruence subgroup Γ₀(N)
description: The subgroup of SL₂(ℤ) consisting of matrices whose lower-left entry is divisible by N, the standard level structure for Hecke theory.

name: Congruence subgroup Γ₁(N)
description: The subgroup of SL₂(ℤ) with lower-left entry ≡ 0 mod N and diagonal entries ≡ 1 mod N, parametrizing modular forms with Nebentypus.

name: Principal congruence subgroup Γ(N)
description: The kernel of SL₂(ℤ) → SL₂(ℤ/Nℤ); a subgroup of SL₂(ℤ) is a congruence subgroup iff it contains some Γ(N).

name: Nebentypus character
description: A Dirichlet character χ mod N in the transformation law f(γz) = χ(d)(cz+d)^k f(z) for forms on Γ₁(N), refining the level structure.

name: Fundamental domain for SL₂(ℤ)
description: The region F = {z ∈ H : |Re(z)| ≤ 1/2, |z| ≥ 1} for the action of SL₂(ℤ) on H, with hyperbolic area π/3.

name: Cusps of a congruence subgroup
description: The Γ-equivalence classes in ℙ¹(ℚ) = ℚ ∪ {∞}, forming the boundary points where Γ\H is compactified to a Riemann surface.

name: Hyperbolic Laplacian on H
description: The Laplace-Beltrami operator Δ = −y²(∂²/∂x² + ∂²/∂y²) on the upper half-plane with Poincaré metric, commuting with SL₂(ℝ).

name: Cusp form
description: A modular form of weight k and level N that vanishes at all cusps, spanning the subspace S_k(Γ) ⊂ M_k(Γ).

name: Slash operator |_k
description: The weight-k right action (f|_k γ)(z) = (cz+d)^{-k} f(γz) of GL₂⁺(ℝ) on functions on H, encoding the modular transformation law.

name: Poincaré series P_m(z, k, Γ)
description: P_m(z) = ∑_{γ ∈ Γ_∞\Γ} e^{2πimγz}(cz+d)^{-k}, spanning cusp forms and satisfying ⟨f, P_m⟩ = c·a_f(m) for cusp forms f.

name: Petersson inner product
description: ⟨f,g⟩ = ∫_{Γ\H} f(z)ḡ(z) y^k dμ(z) on cusp forms, making S_k(Γ) a Hilbert space with Hecke operators self-adjoint.

name: Fourier expansion at cusps
description: The q-expansion f(z) = ∑_{n≥0} a_f(n)e^{2πinz/w} of a modular form at a cusp of width w; the expansion at each cusp determines the form.

name: Atkin-Lehner theory
description: S_k(Γ₀(N)) = S_k^{old} ⊕ S_k^{new} with multiplicity-one for newforms, decomposing cusp forms into oldforms from lower levels and primitive newforms.

name: Atkin-Lehner involution W_Q
description: For Q || N, an involution on S_k(Γ₀(N)) normalizing Γ₀(N); newforms are eigenforms for all W_Q with eigenvalue ±1.

name: Fricke involution W_N
description: The Atkin-Lehner involution z ↦ −1/(Nz) relating the functional equation of L(f,s) to its Fricke eigenvalue.

name: Oldform
description: A form in S_k(Γ₀(N)) arising from lower level M | N via f(z) ↦ f(dz) for d | (N/M), spanning the old subspace.

name: Conductor of a modular form
description: The minimal level N such that a newform lives in S_k(Γ₀(N), χ), encoding the precise ramification data of the associated automorphic representation.

name: Dimension formula for M_k(SL₂(ℤ))
description: dim M_k(SL₂(ℤ)) = ⌊k/12⌋ + 1 for even k ≥ 2 (with correction for k ≡ 2 mod 12), from the Riemann-Roch theorem on the genus-0 modular curve.
aliases: dimension of modular forms for SL₂(ℤ)

name: Dimension formula for S_k(Γ₀(N))
description: dim S_k(Γ₀(N)) = (k−1)(g−1) + corrections from elliptic and parabolic elements, where g is the genus of X₀(N).
aliases: Riemann-Roch dimension formula for cusp forms

name: Theta function of a quadratic form
description: θ_Q(z) = ∑_{n ∈ ℤ^m} e^{2πiQ(n)z} for a positive definite quadratic form Q in m variables; a modular form of weight m/2 whose coefficients count representations by Q.

name: Maass form
description: A smooth Γ-automorphic eigenfunction of the hyperbolic Laplacian Δf = λf on H with at most polynomial growth at cusps.

name: Maass cusp form
description: A Maass form that decays exponentially at all cusps, belonging to the discrete cuspidal spectrum of the Laplacian on L²(Γ\H).

name: Spectral parameter r
description: The parameter r such that a Maass form has eigenvalue λ = 1/4 + r²; the Selberg conjecture asserts r ∈ ℝ for congruence subgroups.

name: Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture
description: For holomorphic cuspidal newforms of weight k, |a_p(f)| ≤ 2p^{(k−1)/2} (Deligne); for Maass forms, |a_p| ≤ 2p^{1/2} (open, best bound from Kim-Sarnak).

name: Real-analytic Eisenstein series E(z,s)
description: E(z,s) = ∑_{γ ∈ Γ_∞\Γ}(Im γz)^s for Re(s) > 1, continued meromorphically to all s, spanning the continuous spectrum of the Laplacian.

name: Scattering matrix for Γ\H
description: The matrix Φ(s) relating constant terms of Eisenstein series at different cusps, satisfying Φ(s)Φ(1−s) = I, whose poles give the residual spectrum.

name: Spectral decomposition of L²(Γ\H)
description: L²(Γ\H) = ℂ ⊕ V_cusp ⊕ V_res ⊕ V_cont, with V_cusp from Maass cusp forms, V_res from residues of Eisenstein series, and V_cont the continuous Eisenstein spectrum.

name: Discrete spectrum of Γ\H
description: The subspace of L²(Γ\H) spanned by eigenfunctions with isolated eigenvalues: constants, Maass cusp forms, and residual Eisenstein contributions.

name: Continuous spectrum of Γ\H
description: The absolutely continuous part of the Laplacian spectrum on L²(Γ\H), parametrized by Eisenstein series E(z, 1/2+it) for t ∈ ℝ, occupying [1/4, ∞).

name: Pre-trace formula
description: ∑_j h(r_j)|u_j(z)|² + (cont. part) = ∑_{γ ∈ Γ} k(u(z,γz)), the spectral expansion of an automorphic kernel, preceding the Selberg trace formula.

name: Selberg zeta function Z_Γ(s)
description: Z_Γ(s) = ∏_{γ₀} ∏_{k≥0}(1 − N(γ₀)^{−s−k}) over primitive hyperbolic classes, an entire function whose zeros encode eigenvalues of Δ on Γ\H.

name: Maass-Selberg relations
description: Inner product formulas for truncated Eisenstein series in terms of the scattering matrix, controlling the continuous spectrum contribution.

name: Petersson trace formula
description: ∑_f ā_f(m)a_f(n)/⟨f,f⟩ = δ_{m,n} + 2πi^{-k}∑_{c≡0(N)} c^{-1}S(m,n;c)J_{k-1}(4π√(mn)/c), relating Fourier coefficients to Kloosterman sums.

name: Eichler-Selberg trace formula
description: An explicit formula for tr(T_n | S_k(Γ₀(N))) as a sum over conjugacy classes involving class numbers, totient values, and cusp/elliptic contributions.
aliases: Selberg trace formula for Hecke operators

name: Kuznetsov trace formula
description: A sum formula relating spectral sums over Maass/holomorphic forms weighted by Fourier coefficients to geometric sums of Kloosterman sums via Bessel transforms.

name: Voronoi summation formula (GL(2))
description: Transforms ∑_n a_f(n)e(nα/q)g(n) for a GL(2) form into a dual sum with Kloosterman twists and Bessel integral transforms; the automorphic Poisson summation.

name: L-function of a modular form
description: L(f,s) = ∑ a_f(n)n^{-s} for a Hecke eigenform f, admitting analytic continuation and functional equation Λ(f,s) = ε·Λ(f,k−s).

name: Euler product for Hecke eigenform L-function
description: L(f,s) = ∏_p(1 − a_p p^{-s} + χ(p)p^{k-1-2s})^{-1} for (p,N) = 1, with modified local factors at primes dividing the level.

name: Rankin-Selberg method
function_signature: (cusp form f, Eisenstein series E(z,s)) → (Rankin-Selberg L-function L(f⊗ḡ,s))
description: Unfolds ∫_{Γ\H} f(z)ḡ(z)E(z,s)y^k dμ to obtain L(f⊗g,s), yielding analytic continuation and bounds for convolution L-functions.

name: Symmetric square L-function L(sym²f, s)
description: The degree-3 L-function ∏_p(1−α²_p p^{-s})^{-1}(1−α_p β_p p^{-s})^{-1}(1−β²_p p^{-s})^{-1} whose analytic properties yield bounds toward Ramanujan.

name: Jacquet-Langlands correspondence
description: A bijection between automorphic representations of GL₂(𝔸) and those of quaternion algebra D×(𝔸) that are not one-dimensional, preserving L-functions.

name: Gelbart-Jacquet lift
description: The functorial lift GL(2)→GL(3) corresponding to the symmetric square, proving L(sym²f,s) is automorphic on GL(3).

name: GL(n) automorphic form
description: A smooth function on GL_n(ℚ)\GL_n(𝔸) satisfying moderate growth, K-finiteness, and Z(g_∞)-finiteness, generalizing classical modular forms.

name: Kirillov model
description: A realization of a generic representation of GL₂(F) on functions on F×, obtained by restricting the Whittaker model to the diagonal torus.

name: Strong multiplicity one for GL(2)
description: Two cuspidal automorphic representations of GL(2) with isomorphic local components at all but finitely many places are globally isomorphic.

name: Twisted L-function L(f⊗χ, s)
description: L(f⊗χ,s) = ∑ a_f(n)χ(n)n^{-s} for a Hecke eigenform f and Dirichlet character χ, with functional equation involving the conductor of χ.

name: Satake parameters
description: The pair (α_p, β_p) with α_p + β_p = a_f(p) and α_p β_p = χ(p)p^{k-1} parametrizing the unramified local factor at prime p via the Satake isomorphism.

name: Hecke multiplicativity relations
description: a(m)a(n) = ∑_{d|(m,n)} χ(d)d^{k-1} a(mn/d²) for a Hecke eigenform, encoding the ring structure of Hecke operators.

name: Amplification method
function_signature: (target form f₀ in spectral family) → (subconvexity bound for L(f₀, 1/2))
description: Constructs an amplifier large on a target form, applies spectral mean-value estimates to convert spectral information into pointwise L-function bounds.

name: Spectral large sieve inequality
description: ∑_j |∑_n a_n ρ_j(n)|² ≤ (N + T²)∑|a_n|², bounding bilinear forms in Fourier coefficients of Maass forms, the spectral analogue of the classical large sieve.

name: Subconvexity for GL(2) L-functions
description: L(f, 1/2) ≪ C(f)^{1/4−δ} for some δ > 0, breaking the convexity bound; proved in various aspects by Iwaniec, Duke-Friedlander-Iwaniec, and Michel-Venkatesh.

name: Mean value estimates via spectral methods
function_signature: (spectral family of L-functions) → (moment asymptotics via Kuznetsov formula)
description: Uses the spectral decomposition and Kuznetsov formula to evaluate moments of L-functions over spectral families.

name: Spectral reciprocity formula
description: An identity relating moments of L-functions over one spectral family to moments over a dual family, transferring subconvexity between aspects.

name: Nonvanishing results for central L-values
description: L(f,1/2) ≠ 0 or L(f⊗χ,1/2) ≠ 0 for a positive proportion of forms/characters in a family, proved via mollified moments.

name: Singular integral (circle method)
description: The archimedean factor J(n) = ∫ δ(x₁^k+…+x_s^k − n) dx in the circle method asymptotic, measuring the real-analytic solution density.

name: Hua's inequality
description: ∫₀¹ |∑_{n≤N} e(αn^k)|^{2^k} dα ≪ N^{2^k − k + ε}, a mean value estimate for Weyl sums fundamental to the minor arc analysis in Waring's problem.

name: Hardy-Littlewood asymptotic for Waring's problem
description: R_{s,k}(n) = 𝔖(n)·J(n)·n^{s/k−1} + o(n^{s/k−1}) for s sufficiently large, where 𝔖 is the singular series and J the singular integral.

name: Farey dissection
function_signature: ([0,1)) → (Farey arcs centered at a/q with q ≤ Q)
description: Partition of [0,1) into arcs centered at Farey fractions of order Q, providing finer major/minor arc decomposition than the standard Hardy-Littlewood dissection.

name: Kloosterman refinement (HLK method)
function_signature: (major arc contributions) → (sums of Kloosterman sums S(m,n;c))
description: The Hardy-Littlewood-Kloosterman method: major arc contributions yield Kloosterman sums whose cancellation (Weil bound) improves the error term.

name: Delta method (Duke-Friedlander-Iwaniec)
function_signature: (binary additive equation n = m) → (smooth delta detection via Kloosterman sums)
description: Replaces the circle method's major/minor arc dissection with a smooth delta symbol built from Kloosterman sums, effective for binary problems.

name: Huxley's zero density estimate
description: N(σ,T) ≪ T^{12(1−σ)/5+ε} for σ ≥ 1/2, improving Ingham's estimate and implying primes in short intervals [x, x + x^{7/12+ε}].

name: Jutila's zero density estimate
description: Improved zero density bounds for Dirichlet L-functions uniform in the conductor q, with applications to primes in arithmetic progressions.

name: Log-free zero density estimate
description: ∑_{χ mod q} N(σ,T,χ) ≪ (qT)^{A(1−σ)} without logarithmic factors, critical for the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem.

name: Zero-detecting polynomial
function_signature: (zeros of L(s,χ)) → (mean value estimate for Dirichlet polynomial M(s)·L(s,χ))
description: A Dirichlet polynomial M(s) chosen so M(s)L(s,χ) ≈ 1 near zeros, converting zero-counting into mean value estimates.

name: Turán's power sum method
function_signature: (power sums of reciprocal zeros) → (lower bound detecting zeros)
description: Bounds max_{1≤ν≤N} |∑ b_j z_j^ν| from below for |z_j| ≥ 1, applied to detect zeros of zeta functions via power sum analysis.

name: Halász-Montgomery method
function_signature: (Dirichlet polynomials near zeros) → (zero density estimates)
description: Combines Halász's theorem on mean values with Montgomery's zero-detection, exploiting duality between zeros and prime distribution.

name: GUE hypothesis for ζ(s) zeros
description: The conjecture that all local statistics of normalized zeros of ζ(s) match those of eigenvalues of large random matrices from the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble.

name: Mollifier method
function_signature: (ζ(s) on critical line) → (lower bound for proportion of zeros at Re(s)=1/2)
description: Multiplies ζ(s) by M(s) ≈ 1/ζ(s) to smooth zeros, then analyzes moments of ζ·M on Re(s)=1/2 to bound zeros on the critical line.

name: Levinson's method
function_signature: (mollifier involving ζ'(s)) → (≥1/3 of zeros on critical line)
description: A refinement of the mollifier method using ζ'/ζ to prove that at least 1/3 of nontrivial zeros of ζ(s) lie on the critical line.

name: Deuring-Heilbronn repulsion phenomenon
description: A real zero β₁ of L(s,χ₁) near 1 forces all other L-functions to have enlarged zero-free regions near 1, with explicit repulsion depending on 1 − β₁.

name: Linnik's constant
description: The infimum L such that the least prime p ≡ a mod q satisfies p ≪ q^L; currently known L ≤ 5 (Xylouris, 2011), and L = 2+ε under GRH.

name: Fouvry's theorem
description: A Bombieri-Vinogradov type result with level of distribution beyond x^{1/2}: for a positive proportion of moduli q ≤ x^{4/7−ε}, the PNT error satisfies strong average bounds.

name: Duke's theorem (equidistribution of CM points)
description: CM points of discriminant −D and closed geodesics of discriminant D become equidistributed on SL₂(ℤ)\H as D → ∞, proved via subconvexity for half-integral weight L-functions.

name: Subconvexity implies equidistribution
description: Subconvexity L(f⊗χ_D, 1/2) ≪ D^{1/4−δ} implies equidistribution of associated arithmetic objects via Weyl's criterion applied to spectral test functions.

name: Erdős-Turán inequality
description: D_N ≤ C(1/H + ∑_{h=1}^H (1/h)|∑_{n≤N} e(hω_n)|/N) for any H ≥ 1, bounding discrepancy by exponential sums.

name: Discrepancy of a sequence
description: D_N = sup_{[a,b)} |#{n ≤ N : ω_n ∈ [a,b)}/N − (b−a)|, the quantitative deviation from uniform distribution.

name: Friedlander-Iwaniec theorem
description: There are infinitely many primes of the form a² + b⁴, proved using the half-dimensional sieve, bilinear forms, and automorphic techniques.

name: Iwaniec's half-dimensional sieve
function_signature: (thin sequence with κ=1/2 sieve dimension) → (prime detection via bilinear structure)
description: A sieve achieving dimension κ = 1/2 by exploiting bilinear structure in error terms, detecting primes where the linear sieve has parity obstruction.

name: Shifted convolution sums
description: Sums ∑_n a_f(n)a_g(n+h) for automorphic coefficients, estimated via spectral methods or the delta method with applications to subconvexity.

name: Additive divisor problem
description: The estimation of ∑_{n≤x} d(n)d(n+h), a prototype shifted convolution sum controlled by spectral theory of automorphic forms.

name: Hecke's converse theorem
description: A Dirichlet series with Euler product and the standard functional equation Λ(s) = εΛ(k−s) necessarily arises from a modular form of weight k for SL₂(ℤ).

name: Weil's converse theorem
description: If L(s,χ) = ∑ a_n χ(n)n^{-s} satisfies functional equations for sufficiently many twists χ, then ∑ a_n q^n is a modular form of the predicted level and character.

name: Holomorphic modular form (weight k, level N)
description: A holomorphic f: H → ℂ with f|_k γ = χ(d)f for all γ ∈ Γ₀(N) and holomorphic at all cusps; M_k(Γ₀(N),χ) is finite-dimensional.

name: Eisenstein series with Nebentypus
description: Eisenstein series E_k(z,χ,ψ) = ∑ χ(c)ψ(d)(cz+d)^{-k} for characters χ,ψ with χψ(-1) = (-1)^k, spanning the Eisenstein subspace of M_k(Γ₁(N)).

name: Ramanujan conjecture for GL(2)
description: The conjecture that for a cuspidal π of GL(2)/ℚ, all unramified local components are tempered; equivalently |α_p| = |β_p| = 1 at Satake parameters.
